rule: Kernel characterization of injectivity for a linear map

conditions.condition: T is a linear map V -> V, so ker(T) is the set of vectors v in V with T(v) = 0.
conditions.justification: The stated linear-map assumption makes the kernel and the zero vector in the claim well-defined.

circularity.justification: The inference uses only the map and injectivity assumptions, not the conclusion or theorem target.

conclusion.justification: If v lies in ker(T), then T(v)=0=T(0); injectivity gives v=0, while linearity gives T(0)=0, so the kernel is exactly {0}.

reason: This is a standard direct consequence of injectivity and the definition of the kernel; finite dimensionality is not needed for this node.
